review: Final forty-one printed spell entries enumerated with neutral keys and source metadata. The three segments cover the stated ninety-three-entry catalogue at first-pass level; cross-reference audit, numeric verification, execution and validation remain pending.

entries.acceptance: First success detects whether one object is magical; a second identifies temporary versus permanent magic. Critical success on either fully identifies the effect as magical analysis does. Preserve observation stage and scope across attempts. Apply recorded spell-class exceptions and shared transaction/ledger rules. Metadata is source inventory, not completed execution.

Reveal personality insight by margin, approximate magical aptitude, possession/control and strong emotions. Critical success reveals concealed supernatural traits. Locate a known individual or manufactured object through a vision, or lead to it within one mile. Knowledge-group spells are instantaneous information unless explicitly given another duration; procedural class still controls roll privacy and payment.
Light/darkness spells affect visible, infrared and ultraviolet channels. Explicit darkness-sight exceptions take precedence over general spectrum blocking.
Mind-group spells do not affect intelligence-zero or free-will-lacking targets; inspect actual actor properties rather than species labels.
Movement-drain is the same cross-listed body spell from B244, not a second purchase or catalogue entry.
Death-group effects apply across ancestries unless a specific ancestry definition overrides eligibility.
Water spells normally cannot affect water inside living beings. Water-breathing is the same cross-listed air spell at B243, not another definition.

The three catalogue segments enumerate ninety-three unique printed spell entries; cross-listed references are not additional entries. Distinct destination versions and the separately listed hostile summoning variant require appropriate identity handling. This count is an inventory target, not proof of implemented completeness.
